claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing can produce an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 while retaining its lamellar character.
This processed architecture improves the strength-ductility combination relative to previously reported reinforcement approaches.
The as-cast alloy has coarser lamellae and larger grains than the proposed processed alloy.
Controlled rolling followed by precise annealing can generate the targeted ultrafine duplex lamellar structure.
The intervention is expected to work only when composition remains near the eutectic point and processing temperature and strain rate lie within an optimized window.
Avoiding excessive grain growth and brittleness is necessary for the proposed processing route to succeed.
The ultrafine duplex microstructure exhibits hierarchical structural constraints.
The processed microstructure provides a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism.
Refined grains increase yield strength through a two-hierarchical constraint effect.
Retained lamellar interfaces deflect and arrest cracks.
The architecture produces a more homogeneous stress distribution.
Constrained deformation slightly increases the effective Young's modulus.
Composite-like behavior enhances ductility and fracture resistance.
The proposed processing will increase yield strength by roughly 20-30% relative to conventional processing.
Fracture toughness will improve by an amount similar to or greater than the predicted yield-strength improvement.
Ductility will be maintained or marginally increased by the proposed processing.
Conventional state-of-the-art processing consists of casting and direct annealing without additional mechanical refinement.
Over-refinement, substantial composition changes, or undesired phase transformations can eliminate the benefit or compromise ductility.
Failure to obtain an approximately 10% or greater statistically significant improvement in both yield strength and fracture toughness without significant ductility loss would falsify the hypothesis.
